newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says employment levels dropped in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Germany says employment levels dropped in 1996.

text.p: The pace of job cuts quickened in Germany last year as the number of people working fell 1.2 percent, underscoring the country's severe unemployment, the German statistics office said Monday.

The Wiesbaden office said the number of people working in Germany -- but not necessarily living in Germany -- fell by 404,000 to 34.5 million from 34.9 million in 1995, when the number of people employed slipped 0.4 percent.

In west Germany, the number fell by 1.1 percent to 28.2 million from 28.5 million. The drop was more significant in the east, where the number of employed fell 1.5 percent to 6.3 million from 6.4 million in 1995.
The loss of jobs in eastern Germany marked a reversal from the 1.1 percent gain in 1995.

The report was issued ahead of Thursday's release of unemployment data for January by the Nuremberg-based German labour office, which was expected to show no improvement from the record unemployment gripping the country.

One German union official said last week she expected the jobless total to rise substantially above 4.4 million for the month compared with the seasonally-adjusted record 4.15 million unemployed in December.

The president of the labour office, Bernhard Jagoda, also said after publication of the December unemployment data that the 4.5 million figure could be reached if the poor weather so far this winter continued into March.
The Wiesbaden report also said the gap between wages in east and west Germany narrowed last year as wage gains in the east more than doubled in manufacturing industry.

Employees in former East Germany were also working longer hours, with the average paid work in manufacturing rising 0.2 percent to 40.3 hours a week, compared with a 2.6 percent drop in the west to 37.9 hours.
